items.evidence: The overview's first section after the title is "## The bottom line", and its three paragraphs run in the required order before "## Findings": "**1. What FRUS answers directly.** The published diplomatic papers answer the question well, and the answer is that there was no single rule...", then "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.** Two channels, which are kept apart and never added together...", then "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.** Four things...". Only a Scope paragraph and the "Decisions this needs from you" list sit between the bottom line and the first finding ("### 1. The baseline of 1900...").

Every quantity names its set and base: "38 documents in 25 volumes, read from a library of 553 volumes"; "for 37 of the 38 documents the index records a source note"; "in the 38 documents' own footnotes there are nine citations in seven documents: six to further decimal files..., two to the Nixon materials'..., and one to a lot file"; "Across the sixteen whole volumes from 1911 to 1945... about 3,400 times, out of about 15,700 footnotes that name a file class"; "turned up in 552 of the 553 volumes, and a nonsense word turned up in none"; "the footnotes of the 25 volumes cite a foreign archive once in about 19,600 footnotes"; "A search of the 1900 to 1912 volumes (about 13,600 documents)"; "about one document in eighteen across the whole library and in about one in eighteen among the 41 volumes titled for the American republics"; "on a sample of forty documents each... matched forty of forty"; "only the first 9,500 of its 33,346 characters were read". No percentage appears anywhere. The remaining digits are years, dates, decimal file numbers (812.00, 837.00, 723.00, 819.01), National Archives identifiers (567985, 567979, 2363840), a lot and entry number (lot 63 D 127, entry A1 3157) and one lot file's own extent ("about three and a half linear feet"), which are identifiers or a named record set's measure, not counts.

All 21 citations give the series title, year, volume where the year has one, and a history.state.gov link, and none is a bare id pair or a title alone; a grep for a frus id outside a historicaldocuments link finds none. The older volumes identify the document by its printed heading and date, e.g. "(Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1921, Volume II, Secretary Hughes's statement of June 8, 1921, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1921v02/d344)", and the modern ones by number, e.g. "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volume XII, American Republics, Document 423, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v12/d423)". Two are weaker, identifying the document only through the link: "(Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1943, The American Republics, Volume V, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1943v05/d34)" and "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1948, The Western Hemisphere, Volume IX, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1948v09/d7)"; neither is a bare id pair nor a title alone, so the item's own no-condition is not met, but a historian with the printed volume would need the link to find those two.

Of the four things listed under "What this request cannot get from FRUS", only (a) names a search: "The searches were for the phrases \"policy of recognition\", \"recognition policy\" and \"question of recognition\", run across the whole library, and the search was shown to work by two controls in the same sitting: the phrase \"Department of State\" turned up in 552 of the 553 volumes, and a nonsense word turned up in none." But the absence it supports, "I read the Department's own statements across eight decades and they do not agree on one list", is a reading judgement, and no count from the three phrases is reported, so the controls validate an engine rather than a measured zero. (b) gives a count with no terms or control: "the footnotes of the 25 volumes cite a foreign archive once in about 19,600 footnotes". (c) is a flat assertion with no search at all: "The working papers of decisions. FRUS prints the decision memoranda and instructions; the staff studies and the Department's daily files behind them are on the decimal-file shelf named above." (d) "Cases not read" is a limit of the run, not an absence from FRUS. No absence is stated with its terms, its volumes, its controls and the zero they make a measurement.

A scan of the overview finds no SQL keyword, no snake_case table or column name, no file path and no frus id outside a history.state.gov link; the only ids present are inside the required links ("https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v12/d423"). The one reference to the working record is by name, not path: "(see the memo for the counts, which are whole-volume, not narrowed to recognition)". The search index is described in words only: "The search index treats words with the same root as the same word, so each phrase was checked in the documents' actual text".

judge:r3.rankingReason: r7 first: a measured census of the whole series (1865 to 1980, 58 documents from a 3,136-document set with per-decade rates), every absence stated as a controlled search with its terms, volumes and counts, full-form citations throughout, and archival leads with catalogue identifiers, entry numbers and access status; it also carries what r3 omits, the 1936 end of the treaty rule, the Legal Adviser's rule and the Carter withholdings, at the cost of very dense paragraphs. r3 second: a clear, well-quoted and well-organized selection of 38 documents stopping in 1973, self-described as \"the best evidence, not a census\", whose bottom line, numbers and citations hold but whose \"cannot get\" rests partly on assertion, with two citations that locate their document only through the link.

refute:r3.notes:
Files present: memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log, plus the session's SQL/scripts and saved outputs. Scratch in /Users/jbotts/frus-analysis/c3/runs/r3/refuter/ (quotecheck.py/.out, ovcheck.py/.out, cites.py/.out, headline.out, identifiers.out, identifiers2.out, usage_recompute.out, footnotes.out, stem_check.out, checker.out, share_check.rerun.out, ctl/ontopic/heads.rerun.out, docs_described.out).

COMMANDS AND RESULTS. (1) python3 -I check_collection.py collection.fruscollection <db> -> '38 documents; all checks pass', exit 0 (the checker verifies format, composition keys, pairs present in document_cache, duplicates and Ed2 twins; it does not check excerpts, which I did myself). (2) quotecheck.py: regex over overview.md for "..." and “...” found 29 quoted strings; 37 excerpt entries all OK at increasing offsets (offsets 200 to 10,051 into the normalised row text); failures 0. (3) ovcheck.py: the 18 overview document quotations checked against the memo-trace pairs, all OK, URL pair == trace pair for all 18; frus1920v03/ch23 header equals the quoted heading. The other 11 quoted strings are not source quotations: 4 search/control phrases ('policy of recognition' present in 1 of the 38 cited rows, 'recognition policy' in 5, 'question of recognition' in 3, 'Department of State' in 17), the user's phrase 'came to power by force' (in the question as posed), the bare word 'recognition' twice, the collection's name (equals the file's name field), and the two NARA labels and the chapter heading already covered; counted as verified for what each claims to be. Total 29 + 37 = 66, verified 66, fabrications 0, mis-citations 0. (4) cites.py: 21 distinct history.state.gov pairs, each resolved to its row, manifest title, header, dateline, document_number and date_iso; all in the collection. (5) headline.out: SQL over the collection's own pairs reproduced 38/25, (553, 321749, 1103, 8481), 37 source rows with frus1900/d530 absent, 9 external_citations rows in 7 docs with the 6/1/2 anchor split. (6) Re-ran ctl.sql, ontopic.sql, heads.sql, extra.sql and share_check.py with sqlite3 -readonly / python3 -I: outputs IDENTICAL to the saved ctl.out, ontopic.out, heads.out, extra.out, share_check.out (552 of 553 volumes hold 'department of state', the one without is frus1919Parisv05, confirmed by my own GROUP BY; ZZZ_IMPOSSIBLE_ZZZ 0; 16,912 and 93,824 of 311,429; 1,527 and 7,197 of 27,240; 13,648 documents in the 15 volumes 1900-1912; 40 of 40 strict and tolerant in all four samples). heads.out: 18 rows, 17 after dropping frus1948v06 (Siam), in 11 volumes, 9 countries (Bolivia 2, Peru 1, Mexico 5, Guatemala 2, Ecuador 1, Cuba 1, El Salvador 2, Argentina 2, Haiti 1) as the overview says. (7) usage_recompute.py, my own code over collection-usage-index.json using the collection's 25 volumes: volumeNoteCounts sum 19,570; by category centralDecimalFile 17,683 ... foreignArchive 1 (in frus1969-76v21); the 16 volumes 1911-1945: 15,671 class-keyed citations, 3,413 matching ^8(1[2-9]|2[0-5]|3[1-9])\.0[01], top keys 812.00 839, 837.00 484, 817.00 357, 818.00 188, 815.00 176, 816.01 169 (812.00 is 326 from frus1913 and 324 from frus1911); the 1910-1949 schedule's country codes 12-39 are all Latin American (12 Mexico ... 39 Dominican Republic; 26-30 absent), so the regex's reading holds. 'About 3,400 of about 15,700', 'about 19,600' and 'once' reproduce; 'one in eighteen' is 311,429/16,912 = 18.41 and 27,240/1,527 = 17.84. (8) Body lengths: 154,469 total for the 38; frus1923v02/d481 = 33,346. (9) frus1948v09/d7: 'Approved by the Secretary of State' is in body_text under the header; the source_note column holds only '800.01/6–845', so the memo's 'in its source note' is loosely put, while the overview's 'approved by the Secretary' holds. frus1913/d894 body: 'Any such formal act of recognition is to be avoided just at the present' supports the overview's paraphrase. frus1958-60v05mSupp/es_d33 source note bears 'Overtaken By Events' as the memo says.

DISCREPANCIES FOUND (none among the five headline numbers, the quotations or the identifiers). (a) A wrong claim in the memo about what was counted: the memo says recogni* is 'porter-stemmed; covers recognize, recognition, recognized'. It does not. frus_documents_vocab: 'recogn' 39,524 docs (the porter stem of recognize/recognized/recognizes), 'recognit' 16,274, 'recognis' 998, 'recogniz' 208; MATCH body_text:recognize -> 38,718 docs, body_text:recogni* -> 16,912, body_text:recognize NOT body_text:recogni* -> 31,435, body_text:recogn* -> 48,348. So the overview's 'the word recognition alone ... about one document in eighteen' counts recognition/recognise/recognizing (1 in 18.4); the token 'recognition' alone is 15,954 (1 in 19.5), and the whole family is 1 in 6.4. The overview's conclusion (the bare word measures the corpus, both sets at the same rate) is unaffected, and the share check's regex 'recogni' matched 40 of 40 as stated, but the memo's coverage statement is a measured error and the 'about one in eighteen' is the stem family's rate, not the word's. (b) frus1921v02/d344: the Hughes statement was made public June 7, 1921; the overview's citation says 'statement of June 8, 1921' (the telegram's date). (c) The memo's use status for lot 63 D 127, 'Unrestricted', decodes under the legend's shared statuses array as us=1 -> 'Other' (the memo read the wrong array); the overview repeats only the access status, which is right. (d) 'Six to further decimal files': d354's and d142's footnote citations name the document's own file number; 'further' is loose, the count is the index's. (e) The overview's '15,700 footnotes that name a file class' is a sum of the usage index's per-class counts; I did not establish whether a footnote carrying two class keys counts once or twice there. (f) The 'Honduras 1907, Haiti 1908 and 1911, Nicaragua 1910' cases are named as found and not followed; only frus1911/d353 of them is in the collection, consistent with the overview's wording.
